note: Mirrored from MAC League's public coaching-resources pages (Majors Rules, General Rules, Playoff Rules). Re-check this content each offseason or when the league announces a mid-season rule change -- these are infrequent enough that a periodic manual re-pull is enough, no live scraping needed.

rules.text: The ball is always live.

Each inning has a limit of 5 runs per team. When the fifth run crosses the plate, that half of the inning ends and the team at bat takes the field. This rule does not apply to the 6th or last inning where both teams can score unlimited runs. The umpire must notify the coaches before the start of the last inning.
For those teams playing in Major-A games, there is no per-inning run limit.

On deck batters are allowed behind the 3rd or 1st base coaches, or preferably outside the field of play. Coaches will be responsible for understanding and administering where on deck batters are allowed to warm up. Check with the home team coach for in-town specific rules that must be followed.
Every team member must be in a consistent batting order. The batting order may not change during a game.
Games will be played on a diamond with 70' base paths.
Towns are allowed to but not required to use a double safety bag at first base. All towns will be required to use a double first base starting in the Spring of 2027. (Updated 2/27/26)
All players must use a bat that has been certified by USABat. BBCOR or USSSA bats are not allowed. Coaches are responsible for ensuring their players are using approved bats.

Any player throwing equipment, with malice, will get a warning the first time it happens. The second time, the player will be automatically ejected from the game. The umpire may eject the player on the first incident if they determine the level of malice warrants an immediate ejection.

Any player throwing a bat, without malice, will get a warning the first time it happens. The second time, the player will be called out, and must then be removed from the batting lineup for the remainder of the game. The player can and should still play on defense. When that person's spot in the lineup comes up the next time, the slot should simply be skipped, and no out should be recorded.

There shall be no slashing. Slashing is defined as: the pitcher is on the pitching rubber and the batter fakes a bunt to draw the infielders in and then the batter swings away. The pitcher does not need to be in his windup, the ball does not need to be struck. Penalty: Batter is out, and ball is dead. A second offense will result in the batter being ejected.

The slide or avoid rule is in effect. It is mandatory that a base runner slides or avoids when there is an imminent play at second, third base or home plate. The base runner, at the sole discretion and judgment of the umpire, should be called out for not sliding or avoiding or if contact is made.
Players hit by a pitch will be awarded first base, and the batter must take first base (if a batter is hurt and unable to run, he/she may be replaced by the last person that was called out).
If a player's bat contacts the ball with any part of their body touching outside of the batter's box, they will be called out immediately.
Both headfirst sliding into a forward base (including home) and headfirst sliding to a previously occupied base is now allowed. (Updated 2/27/2026)
Outfielders are not allowed to play within the infield limits. They should never be standing on the infield dirt.
There is no limit to the number of bases a runner may steal or advance to on passed balls/wild pitches.
Runners may leave the base anytime as the ball is live. This includes runners taking a lead and attempting to steal any base (except 1st base) before, during or after a pitch.

Infield fly rule: a fair fly ball (not a line drive, nor an attempted bunt) catchable by an infielder with ordinary effort, when 1st+2nd or 1st+2nd+3rd are occupied with fewer than two outs. The pitcher, catcher and any outfielder stationed in the infield count as infielders for this rule. The umpire must immediately declare 'Infield Fly' (or 'Infield Fly, if Fair' near the baseline); the ball stays live and runners may advance at the risk of it being caught. If it falls untouched and goes foul before 1st/3rd, it's a foul ball; if it falls fair, the infield fly call stands regardless.

Dropped third strike: a batter may advance to 1st on a dropped 3rd strike any time 1st base is unoccupied (out on a force or tag). When 1st is occupied, a batter may ONLY advance on a dropped 3rd strike with two outs. As soon as a player steps outside the dirt circle they are out; until then they can turn and run to first.
Two adult base coaches are permitted -- rostered coaches or CORI non-rostered adults. Rostered players may also base coach, but must wear a helmet.
When there are two outs a courtesy runner for catchers is allowed and should be used whenever possible. A courtesy runner must be the last person who made an out.
Leading is allowed.
At the start of each extra inning, a runner is placed on second base -- the runner will be the last recorded batter of the previous inning. (Added 2/1/2026)

All players must be in the game for 6 defensive outs (regulation 6-inning games). Failure results in an automatic forfeit by the non-complying team, except in a shortened game (darkness, weather, etc.), where it does not.
Free defensive substitutions are allowed between innings.
Teams will be playing with three outfielders: a left fielder, center fielder and right fielder.
The distance of the pitching mound to home plate is 50 feet.

MAC League follows MLB/USA Baseball Pitch Smart Guidelines for pitch counts and days of rest. Players cannot pitch in multiple games on the same day. Once removed from pitching, a player may not return as a pitcher for that game. No pitcher shall appear as a pitcher for three consecutive days (not games), regardless of pitch count.
Recommendation for safety: players should avoid catching and pitching during the same game, and should count pitches/appearances for outside teams as if it was the same team.
If a pitcher hits 4 players total within a game (not necessarily one inning), that player must be removed from pitching for the remainder of the game.
Pitching substitution may happen mid-inning and does NOT need to be 1-for-1 (e.g. Johnny replaced by Billy, Billy by Bobby, Bobby by Johnny).
A new pitcher gets 6 warmup pitches; returning pitchers get only 4 warmup pitches between innings, to speed up the game.
Only coaches, assistants or team members may warm up the pitcher, and must wear a helmet to do so (adults exempt).

Any mound visit by a coach after the first pitch and before the last out counts as an official visit. On the second visit of the inning the pitcher must be removed, though the umpire may allow extra visits for a player health check.

All balks are called warnings, except for Major-A games, where only the 1st balk for a pitcher is a warning -- any subsequent balk awards runners a base. A called balk is always a dead ball; runners return to their original bases. (Updated 5/2/2025)
(Summer & Fall) Each pitcher is limited to 3 innings maximum per game.

(Spring) Pitch counts must be recorded (manual counter or electronic device/app) and reported to the league within 24 hours of the game. If coaches' counts disagree, the electronic-device coach's count is official.

(Spring) If a pitcher reaches their daily max mid-at-bat, they MAY finish that batter before being pulled -- but may NOT finish the batter if doing so would cross into the next day's-rest threshold (unless the coach accepts the longer rest requirement).
(Spring) Majors pitch count / rest requirements -- Daily Max 85. No Rest: 1-20 pitches. 1 Day Rest: 21-35. 2 Days Rest: 36-50. 3 Days Rest: 51-65. 4 Days Rest: 66+.

If a Majors game is played at a field without 70' base paths: no leading, runners may not leave until the ball crosses the plate, no delayed steals, pitching distance 46', base distance 60'. Playoff games must be played on a field with 70' base paths.
(Spring) Weeknight games start at 5:45pm (Rookie games at 6pm, shorter game time).
(Spring) If a team cannot field at least 8 players within 15 minutes of the scheduled start, it is scored a forfeit (loss), recorded as 6-0.

Rule violations: 1st offense against a team is a warning, 2nd is reviewed for severity (leaning warning unless egregious), 3rd is a forfeit. The MAC board may rule outside these guidelines by majority vote when deemed necessary.
Only coaches may use electronic devices/cell phones during games. There are NO protests allowed at any level.

No new inning may start after 2 hours (Minors & Majors) or 2 hours 30 minutes (Juniors & Seniors) from the official start time, which the umpire announces at the start of the game. Games may start early if both teams and the umpire are ready. The umpire may call the game earlier for weather, darkness, or other circumstances.

Both teams get a 10-minute pre-game practice on the field. Visiting teams should arrive 30 minutes before game time; home team warms up first but must allow the visiting team to begin warmups 20 minutes before start. No pre-game, on-field batting practice is allowed. Example for a 6pm start: home arrival by 5:20pm (warm up 5:30-5:40), visiting arrival by 5:30pm (warm up 5:40-5:50), coaches/umpire pregame conference at 5:50pm, home team takes the field by 5:55pm, first pitch by 6:00pm.
During the pregame conference, coaches must tell the umpire which players are ineligible to pitch due to prior pitch counts/innings.
The home team pays the umpire(s), supplies 2 new game balls, and keeps the field in safe condition. Each team cleans trash from their own bench area after the game.

Game length: 6-inning limit for Minors & Majors, 7-inning limit for Juniors & Seniors, unless tied (extra innings required). A game called mid-inning reverts to the score at the end of the previous inning.

Mercy rule -- Minors: conceded if one team leads by 12+ after the 3rd, or 8+ at/after the top of the 4th (immediate if the home team goes up 8+ in the bottom of the 4th). Majors: 15+ after the 3rd, or 10+ at/after the top of the 4th (immediate if home team goes up 10+ in bottom of 4th). Juniors & Seniors: 10+ after the 4th, or 8+ at/after the top of the 5th (immediate if home team goes up 8+ in bottom of 5th).

(Spring) If a mercy is called, the win is conceded and the score at that moment is final/official for the website -- no further scorekeeping. Play may continue informally to a natural end under a 2-run-per-inning limit at all levels, and pitching stats/pitch counts must still be recorded.

(Spring) The winning coach must post the score on the MAC League website within 24 hours or before the next scheduled game, whichever comes first. Both teams must report every player's pitches thrown (first name, last initial, uniform number, total pitches) regardless of win or loss.
(Spring) A pitch-count rule violation must be reported immediately to the MAC board -- 1st violation is a warning, 2nd causes forfeiture of that game.

Teams short on players may add CALL UP players, up to a game-day roster of 10. (Spring) CALL UPs must come from a lower division only. (Summer & Fall) CALL UPs may come from a lower division, the same division, or even be borrowed from the other team.

CALL UP players may pitch, but any pitches/innings count against their own rostered team's limits. They go at the bottom of the lineup and never get priority over rostered players -- outside the 6 required defensive outs, a rostered player shouldn't sit while a CALL UP plays the field.

A game should NEVER be cancelled for any reason other than weather -- use the CALL UP system for scheduling conflicts. (Spring) A cancelled game must get a makeup date arranged within 24 hours of the original date or season's end, whichever is first, played as close to the original date as possible.

The home team gets first chance to arrange the makeup field; if they can't within 2 days, the visiting team may schedule it on their own field (original home team stays 'home'). (Spring) Games not played/unreported by season's end are ignored -- no points or runs awarded either way. If coaches can't agree on a new date, the original date stands and a no-show team forfeits.

rules.section: Rain Outs / Incomplete Games / Lightning / Darkness
rules.text: In bad weather, the home coach must call the umpire and visiting coach 2 hours before the scheduled start. No game should be called more than 2 hours before start; coaches should try to get the game in through light/moderate rain. After the first pitch, only umpires can cancel a game.

rules.section: Rain Outs / Incomplete Games / Lightning / Darkness
rules.text: A game becomes official/regulation after the 4th inning (or 3.5 innings if the home team is ahead). Postponed before/during the 1st inning: restarts fresh at an agreed time. Postponed after the 2nd and before the 4th is complete: resumes where it stopped. All stats, including pitch counts, must still be counted even in a cancelled/postponed game.

rules.section: Rain Outs / Incomplete Games / Lightning / Darkness
rules.text: Lightning: the game stops immediately and all players seek covered shelter; it may not resume until at least 15 minutes after the last visible lightning. This applies whenever the umpire OR either head coach sees lightning, not just the umpire. If a team no longer has enough players when play resumes, it's a forfeit.

rules.section: Rain Outs / Incomplete Games / Lightning / Darkness
rules.text: A game called early reverts to the score at the end of the previous inning; pitch counts are NOT rolled back and must be reported as of when the game was called. A rain delay extends the game's time limit by the length of the delay.

All batters and base runners must wear a batting helmet; youth base coaches must always wear helmets. No watches, rings, pins, necklaces, jewelry or other metallic items (medically relevant bracelets excepted). Pitchers may not wear wristbands/sweatbands.

Rookie, Minors & Majors players must wear plastic cleats; metal cleats only in Juniors & Seniors. Baseball Rookie/Minors/Majors require a USABat-stamped bat; Juniors & Seniors require BBCOR-certified (13-14-year-olds still use USABat, though not recommended). Softball requires a bat stamped 'Official Softball Bat' or 'Official Fastpitch Bat'.

Solid one-piece wood bats are permitted in all divisions (must conform to Babe Ruth Rule 1.10); no laminated or experimental bats. USSSA bats are not allowed in any division. MAC League does not enforce Babe Ruth's 12.5" glove-size limit.
Towns may optionally use a double safety bag at first base; it becomes mandatory league-wide starting Spring 2027. (Updated 2/27/26)

Arguing with an umpire: the umpire calls over both coaches for a warning to the offending person; if it continues, the person is ejected and serves at least a one-game suspension at the town level. A second ejection after that may be recommended as a season-long suspension.
A coach may never yell at a player on another team -- any issue goes through the other coach or the umpire only. Doing so means ejection plus a one-game suspension.
Coaches should not accept helmet-throwing, arguing with umpires, heckling, or similar behavior from players, and must address it immediately. Teams line up and shake hands after every game.

Taunting of opposing players, coaches, or umpires is prohibited under Cal Ripken/Babe Ruth rules. Positive chanting/cheering for your own team is encouraged, but all noise must stop the moment the pitcher starts their windup.

Umpires call balls/strikes and safe/out on the bases; no disputing any call. A rule-interpretation question may be raised with the umpire after the inning, but the umpire's decision is final and binding.
An umpire may stop active play at any time (e.g. an injury), at their discretion -- if they don't stop play, the ball stays live.

Home team pays the umpire(s), ideally before the game starts. (Spring) rates: Minors Junior Umps $30 each (2) or $40 (1 Senior); Senior Umps $60; Majors $90 (1 Senior); Juniors $100 (1 Senior); Seniors $75 each (2 Senior). (Summer & Fall) rates: Majors/Juniors $80 (1 Senior), others same as Spring.

Junior Umpires: 12+ years old, may or may not hold current Babe Ruth certification; if 18+, must have passed MA CORI + SafeSport. Not eligible for postseason games. Senior Umpires: 15+ years old, must hold current Babe Ruth certification; if under 21, need 2+ years/5+ games of umpiring experience; if 18+, must have passed MA CORI + SafeSport.

Junior Umpires should be used whenever possible in Minors & Offseason Majors (two umpires scheduled when Juniors are planned), may never work a playoff/tournament game, and must stay unbiased (no team-branded clothing/hats).

For a Majors-and-up game, if the home team can't field a Senior umpire, the home team forfeits (the game can still be played as a scrimmage with Junior Umpires, parents, or coaches). Umpire performance issues should go to the local league's umpire coordinator first, who escalates to the MAC board if needed.

All regular-season rules apply in the playoffs except where noted here. Only the Spring Season, Minors-and-up divisions play in the end-of-season playoff tournament, a single-elimination bracket starting immediately after the regular season.
Standings freeze at 8pm on the final day of the season; any score not entered by then is recorded as DNP (Did Not Play).

Standings/seeding are determined, in order, by: most points (3/win, 2/tie, 1/loss, 0/forfeit-loss*); head-to-head (skipped if 3+ teams are tied unless one is undefeated against the others); total runs if games-played is equal, else average runs/game; Runs Against; Runs For; coin flip. *Forfeit-losses currently can't be distinguished in the system, so they count as a 1-point loss for now.
Once final seedings are announced they are final; a post-release error can only be corrected by a majority MAC board vote.

A team unable to field enough players can ask the opposing coach to move the game earlier than the league's next scheduled date; pitch-count rules aren't adjusted for moved games. If both teams don't agree to a new date, the original stands and the short-handed team forfeits.
A forfeit less than 48 hours before the scheduled start lets the bracket proceed as planned; a forfeit more than 48 hours out lets the MAC board (majority vote) decide whether to reseed.

The higher seed is always the home team and hosts (gets umpires, provides 2 game balls). North/South home-field ties follow the league point system, then a coin flip. No re-seeding once the tournament begins.
If a team can't field 9 players, CALL UP players are allowed from a younger division only, may NOT pitch, must play outfield only, and go at the bottom of the lineup.

A playoff game hitting the mercy rule ends immediately. Otherwise all playoff games play to a natural end; an incomplete game is suspended and continued later. Score and pitch counts must be reported on the MAC website immediately after the game.

Championship and division-final (or semi-final) games require two patched umpires at regular-season rates; all other tournament games require one. No unpatched umpires allowed. All Minors playoff games pay umpires at the Major-level rate.

During the whole playoff tournament, umpire costs are split evenly between the two teams at standard MAC pricing (each coach brings their half); a town choosing to pay more covers that difference itself.

If a game is suspended for weather: a pitcher already pulled before the stoppage can't return to pitch when play resumes. A pitcher still in the game at the stoppage keeps their pitch count and continues it when play resumes (e.g. 29 at suspension -> next pitch is #30), with the final count recorded as suspension-count plus pitches thrown after resuming. If that pitcher doesn't continue pitching on resumption, they're done pitching for the rest of the game. Any other pitcher follows normal playoff rest rules based on calendar days since they last pitched.
All pitch counts reset at the start of the playoff tournament. Breaking the pitch-count rules in the playoffs automatically forfeits that game.
Minors -- Daily Max 75. No Rest: 1-20. 1 Day Rest: 21-40. 2 Days Rest: 41-65. 3 Days Rest: 66+.
Majors -- Daily Max 85. No Rest: 1-20. 1 Day Rest: 21-40. 2 Days Rest: 41-65. 3 Days Rest: 66+.
Juniors -- Daily Max 95. No Rest: 1-25. 1 Day Rest: 26-45. 2 Days Rest: 46-65. 3 Days Rest: 66+.
Seniors -- Daily Max 105. No Rest: 1-30. 1 Day Rest: 31-45. 2 Days Rest: 46-65. 3 Days Rest: 66+.
